explanation: The capital city of ancient Israel and Judah, a central place for worship and political power.
A Jewish leader who helped rebuild Jerusalem and strengthen the community after the exile in Babylon.
The process of restoring something that has been destroyed or damaged, in this case Jerusalem and its wall.
A holy place where people worshipped God, especially the first temple in Jerusalem built by King Solomon.
Members of the tribe of Levi who had special religious duties and responsibilities connected to the temple and worship.
Religious leaders from the line of Aaron who were responsible for performing ceremonies and sacrifices in the temple.
People living in a specific area or city, in this case those who lived in Jerusalem and other towns in Judah.
A method for randomly selecting people or things, used in Nehemiah 11 to determine who should live in Jerusalem.
Showing reverence and devotion toward a deity, in this case the Almighty God.
